entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.10：声音也活过了存档
entry.content:
那段留在后面的音乐​

你在 boss 打到一半的时候按了存档。音乐正响，那只大家伙正在做一件让人难受的事，你把手机放下，去回一条消息。

两分钟后你回来，读档。

战斗和你离开时一模一样——怪物、血条、它的坐标，样样都对。可音乐完全不在同一条时间线上：它从来没有跟机器一起被冻住，于是一切都倒回去了，它还在往前放。而 PC 喇叭那头的哔哔声还在后台嗡嗡地响，谁也不理。

那是 1.0.0.9。存档做得很好，好到只差一样东西：声音。

存档存的是一台机器，不是一块屏幕​

存档本来应该存下整台机器：CPU、内存、显存、打开的 DOS 文件句柄、硬件定时器。少了机器的任何一个部件，读回来就只是一台略有不同的机器——而这一次，你听得出来。

FM 芯片根本不在快照里。不是存得不准、不是存得不全——是压根没有。

这比听上去更糟，因为游戏冻住的时候芯片并不会跟着停。游戏运行中读档，模拟器会把它知道的一切倒回去：怪物、血条、那只大家伙的坐标、DOS 文件句柄、定时器。芯片不在它知道的那一串里，于是它继续放下去。你眼前是一场被倒带的战斗，耳朵里却是没有倒带的音乐。

如果这份存档是被恢复进一个全新的进程里——也就是关掉应用之后再按继续时发生的事——那芯片是崭新的、空白、哑的，音乐直接就没了。

PC 喇叭坏得又是第三种方式。它确实在快照里，可它是个实时输出设备，它排队的延迟和定时器索引被按着当前时钟恢复，而不是被保存时的那台机器的时钟——于是混音器继续发出一个客人根本没要求过的蜂鸣。它带着嗡声回来了。

「精确」在这里是什么意思​

修法是把芯片本身整个存下来，而不是存它的摘要。OPL 的状态是一个大约五千字节的结构体：每个运算单元的包络、波形相位、LFO 计数器、反馈历史。它被写进状态文件、再读回来，于是下一个采样点从上一个采样点停下的地方接着走。

还有一种更省事的做法，值得说清楚它为什么不够用。这个移植留着芯片的 512 个寄存器——驱动把音色写进去的那些——读档时可以重放它们。这能把音色完美地重建出来。但驱动在一首曲子的开头把音色编好，之后只发「按下」和「松开」；在这中间发生的一切都活在芯片内部，没有任何一个寄存器记录得了。于是重放寄存器就等于把每一个音符都从攻击段重新触发。音回来了，却回错了：它从头开始，而不是从原来的地方接着走。

所以寄存器重放还在，作为那些无法快照自己的 OPL 模型的兜底。但它现在只是兜底，不再是主方案。

我是怎么验的​

我让自己相信这件事成立的方式，是我希望自己被说服的方式：写一个测试程序，在 FM 芯片上编出一个持续的长音，然后等一个按键。

OPL 测试包：一个持续的长音，以及一行提示——存一个档，等一等，再读回来。

这个测试包就在仓库里，你也可以自己跑。屏幕上就写着它是什么："The tone is playing. Press any key to stop it."

然后这个移植在存档时把芯片的状态打进日志，读档时再打一遍，两边必须对得上——同样的包络、同样的波形相位、同样的 LFO 计数器、同样的寄存器内容。

这是相隔两分钟真实芯片时间的存档日志和读档日志：

savestate: OPL chip saved:    ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module saved:  exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

savestate: OPL chip restored: ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module restored: exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

一模一样。音从攻击段中间接上，继续响。

有件事你得知道​

1.0.0.9 写下的存档，1.0.0.10 读不了了。

声音芯片进了快照之后，状态文件多了一个版本号，读档端现在会拒绝旧存档，而不是硬把它读错。这才是诚实的做法——一个能读、但声音读错的存档，比一个直接说「不行」的存档更糟糕。

如果你手上有 1.0.0.9 留下的存档在意，升级之前先读出来。

一个一直按着的键​

按着某个键的时候转屏，那个键会永远按在 DOSBox 里。旋转之后布局要重建，而重建出来的布局没有告诉模拟器「手指已经抬起来了」，于是那个键一直按着，DOSBox 就一直重复它。

现在，布局重建时，所有处于按下状态的键都会被释放。

还有另一半。Ctrl 同时出现在两个地方——手柄区和折叠面板上——而代码默认它上面永远只有一根手指，于是在一处松开会把另一处也取消掉。现在它会数手指。

塞得下的启动器​

Files 面板现在会量一量自己有多少空间，再据此限制游戏列表的数量。以前装到第三个游戏，按钮会被挤出面板底边——掉下去就再也捞不回来了。

这是这一版里最小的改动，也是我最恼火它没在前三个版本里就发生的一个。

桌面版又能链接了​

存档相关的代码从来没被加进 autotools 的构建里，所以那个桌面基线——也就是那个能在笔记本上几秒钟编完、用来盯着模拟器内核别走偏的构建——从 1.0.0.8 引入存档开始就链接不过了。

我为这件事蒙了整整两个版本，因为我忙着发安卓版，一直没顾上。

原因有四条，彼此独立，但其实是同一类：构建里漏了一个源文件、少了一个头文件、一个函数本来该被条件编译掉、以及同一个静态库被连着列了两次——那是一个循环依赖，换个顺序才会暴露。

现在基线又能编译链接，也能跑。

一份文档，而不是一本流水账​

仓库过去有一个 porting/ 目录：一份移植日志、一些跑分笔记、一份键盘设计说明，还有一个日志文件。还在写移植的时候它们很有用；写完之后就没用了，因为那是按时间顺序记下来的东西——你得先知道事情发生的先后，才知道现在哪一条是真的。

现在只剩一份参考文档：docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md。整个实现都在这一个地方——原生构建和 ABI 矩阵、存档机制和它的文件格式、精确的 FM 快照、快照里的 DOS 层、启动器、屏幕键盘、吞吐跑分、还有哪些东西没被拍进去，以及这个移植拍下的每一张截图，都带着源码引用。

流水账没有消失，它变成了章节。历史仍然在 git log 里，那本来就是历史该待的地方。

安卓移植结束了​

这一版带了一个不是版本号的标签：

milestone/android-migration-complete

它是带注释的，曾经指向这一版的提交（这个标记后来移到了 v1.0.0.11），而且故意落在发布脚本能理解的 vX.Y.Z.A 格式之外，所以脚本永远不会再把它当成一次发布捡起来。

它标记的是一个阶段，不是一个版本。安卓移植已经完成：模拟器核心能为三个 ABI 编译，应用层在真机上跑得动，存档装得下整台机器——包括声音——桌面基线也能链接了。接下来是维护：修 bug 和打磨文档。没有新功能的计划。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 就在仓库里，用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装 1.0.0.9：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.10

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.10.apk
sha256: 80bdce1b4bdeba809159310441e450e704f6c322e2a3ff98bcc822ed50077018

GitHub Release 上另有一份由流水线在干净机器上构建的产物，旁边带着它自己的 SHA-256 文件。

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身，而且现在是一份参考文档，不再是一堆笔记。请去读那份，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

一个听不见的存档只能算半个存档。正是这件事让我给一颗声音芯片写了个测试程序。如果你的存档读回来时音乐对不上——或者干脆没了——这一版就是你要的那一版。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.10: the sound survives the save state
entry.content:
The music that stayed behind​

You freeze a game in the middle of a fight. The music is loud, the boss is doing something unpleasant, and you put the phone down to answer a message.

You come back two minutes later and load the state.

The fight is exactly where you left it — the sprites, the health bar, the position of the boss, all of it. The music, though, is somewhere else entirely: it was never frozen with the rest of the machine, so it carried on playing while everything else went back. And the beeping that was coming out of the PC speaker is still going on in the background, droning at nobody.

That was 1.0.0.9. The snapshot was very good, and it was missing the sound.

A save state is a machine, not a screen​

A save state is supposed to be the whole machine: the CPU, the memory, the video memory, the open DOS file handles, the hardware timers. If one part of the machine is missing from the snapshot, the machine you come back to is a slightly different machine, and you can hear it.

The FM chip was not in the snapshot. Not badly, not approximately — not at all.

That is worse than it sounds, because the chip does not stop while the game is frozen. Load a state while the game is running and the emulator rewinds everything it knows about: the sprites, the health bar, the boss's coordinates, the DOS file handles, the timers. The chip is not among the things it knows, so it keeps playing. You are looking at a fight that has been rewound, and listening to music that has not.

And if the state is restored into a fresh process — which is what the Resume button does after the app has been closed — the chip is new, blank and silent, and the music is simply gone.

The PC speaker was a third kind of broken. It was in the snapshot, but it is a real-time output device, and its queued delays and its timer indices were restored against the current clock rather than the saved one — so the mixer carried on emitting a beep the guest had never asked for. It came back droning.

What "exactly" means here​

The fix is to snapshot the chip itself — the whole thing, not a summary of it. The OPL's state is a single struct of about five kilobytes: the envelope of every operator, the wave phase, the LFO counters, the feedback history. It is written into the state file and read back, so the next sample continues from where the last one stopped.

There is a cheaper version of this, and it is worth explaining why it is not enough. The port keeps a copy of the chip's 512 registers — the ones the driver wrote its instruments into — and a restore can replay them. That rebuilds the instruments perfectly. But a driver programs its instruments once at the start of a song and then only says key on and key off; everything that happens in between lives inside the chip, where no register records it. Replaying the registers therefore re-triggers every note from its attack. The tone comes back — but it comes back wrong: it starts again instead of continuing where it was.

So the register replay is still here, as the fallback for the OPL models that cannot snapshot themselves. But it is a fallback now, not the plan.

How I checked it​

The way I convinced myself this works is the way I would want to be convinced: I wrote a test program that programs one sustained tone on the FM chip and then waits for a key.

The OPL test bundle: one sustained tone, and an instruction to save a state, wait, and load it again.

The bundle is in the repository, so you can run it yourself. It says what it is on the screen: "The tone is playing. Press any key to stop it."

Then the port writes the chip's state to the log when it saves, and writes it again when it loads, and the two have to match — same envelope, same wave phase, same LFO counter, same register contents.

Here they are, two minutes of live chip time apart:

savestate: OPL chip saved:    ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module saved:  exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

savestate: OPL chip restored: ... phase=d96f49ac ... active=36 lfo=000b228c opl3=0
savestate: OPL module restored: exact=1 mode=2 regs=62/512 r20=31 r23=31 r40=3f ...

Identical. The tone picked up in the middle of its attack and carried on.

One consequence you should know about​

Save states written by 1.0.0.9 cannot be loaded by 1.0.0.10.

The state file grew a version when the sound chips became part of the snapshot, and the loader now refuses an older state rather than misreading it. That is the honest behaviour — a state that loads but plays the wrong sound is worse than a state that says no.

If you have save states from 1.0.0.9 that you care about, load them before you update.

A key that stayed down​

Rotating the phone while a key was held left that key pressed in DOSBox for ever. The layout is rebuilt on a rotation, and the rebuilt layout did not tell the emulator that the finger had come up — so the key stayed down, and DOSBox went on repeating it.

Now every key that is down is released when the layout is rebuilt.

There was a second half to it. Ctrl is shown in two places at once — on the pad and on the fold-up panel — and the code assumed there was only ever one finger on it, so releasing it in one place cancelled it in the other. It now counts the fingers.

The launcher that fits​

The Files panel measures the space it has and caps the game list to it. A third game used to push the buttons off the bottom edge of the panel, where nothing could bring them back.

This is the smallest change in the release and the one I am most annoyed did not happen in the first three.

The desktop build links again​

The save-state code was never added to the autotools build, so the desktop baseline — the build that keeps the emulator core honest, the one that compiles on a laptop in seconds — had stopped linking. It had been broken since the save states went in, in 1.0.0.8, and I did not notice for two releases because I was busy shipping the Android one.

There were four separate reasons, and they are all of the same kind: a source file missing from the build, a missing include, a function that should have been compiled out, and the same archive listed twice in a row, which is a circular dependency that only shows up in a particular order.

The baseline compiles and links again, and it runs.

One document instead of a diary​

The repository used to carry a porting/ folder: a porting log, some bench notes, a design note for the keyboard, and a log file. It was useful while the port was being written and it had stopped being useful the moment it was finished, because it was a chronicle — you had to know the order of things to know what was true now.

There is now one reference document: docs/TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md. It is the whole implementation in one place — the native build and the ABI matrix, the save-state machine and its file format, the exact FM snapshot, the DOS layer inside the snapshot, the bundle launcher, the on-screen keyboard, the throughput benchmark, what is still not captured, and every screenshot the port produced, with the source references inline.

The diary did not disappear; it became chapters. The history is still in the git log, where history belongs.

The Android migration is over​

This release carries a tag that is not a release:

milestone/android-migration-complete

It is annotated, it pointed at this release's commit — the marker has since moved on to v1.0.0.11 — and it deliberately sits outside the vX.Y.Z.A scheme the release script understands, so the script will never pick it up and try to release it again.

It marks a phase, not a version. The Android migration is done: the emulator core builds for three ABIs, the app layer works on a real device, save states carry the whole machine including the sound, and the desktop baseline links. What comes after this is maintenance — bug fixes and documentation polish. No new features are planned.

Get it​

The release APK is in the repository, signed with the release key, so it installs over 1.0.0.9 in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.10

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.10.apk
sha256: 80bdce1b4bdeba809159310441e450e704f6c322e2a3ff98bcc822ed50077018

The GitHub Release carries its own asset, built by the pipeline on a clean runner, with its own SHA-256 file next to it.

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository, and it is now a single reference document rather than a folder of notes. Please read that rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

A save state that cannot hear is only half a save state. That is what made me write a test program for a sound chip. If your states came back with the music out of sync — or gone entirely — this is the release you want.

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox：昨日的计算世界，今日的掌上体验，明日的无限可能
entry.content:
还记得那个没有应用商店、没有触摸屏、没有云账号的年代吗？但我们依然可以为了玩一款游戏，心甘情愿地耗上整个周末。😂

那时候，我们敲着 C:\GAMES\DOOM.EXE，就觉得自己已经是计算机专家了。

其实，DOS 从未真正离开。它只是在等待一台更小的电脑。

今天，我们希望通过 WhereQ-DOSBox，让这段经典的计算机世界在 Android 手机上继续延续。

它不是运行在浏览器里的 DOS 模拟器，也不是连接到某台老电脑的远程桌面。它是一个原生 Android 应用，真正的 DOSBox 模拟器核心以原生动态库的形式集成在 APK 内部。

而它背后，还有不少值得分享的东西。

眼见为实​

手机上的 WhereQ-DOSBox：中间跑着 FIFA 96，左右两条黑边里是两块手柄区， 底下垫着 1990 年世界杯的那首歌。屏幕上的一切都是真正的 DOSBox 核心， 以原生动态库的形式跑在 APK 内部。

不只是运行 DOS 游戏​

原生 Android 架构​

基于 DOSBox r4305 和 SDL2，通过 Android NDK 与 CMake 集成构建。原生支持 ARM64、ARMv7 和 x86_64 架构。

智能 CPU 执行机制​

通过 core=auto 配置，普通实模式程序自动使用解释执行，而进入保护模式的程序则切换到动态重编译（JIT）执行。DOS/4GW 程序也在我们的兼容性探索范围之内。

真正理解手机操作的键盘​

DOS 游戏是为键盘设计的，而不是为手指设计的。我们没有简单地把一块桌面键盘缩小后塞进手机屏幕。

横屏模式下，4:3 的 DOS 显示区域保持在屏幕中央，常用控制按键则充分利用左右两侧的黑边区域。竖屏模式则采用紧凑的底部键盘布局。

你的 DOS 环境，你的程序​

支持导入 ZIP 游戏包、从文件夹批量安装，也可以直接通过 Android 文件管理器打开 ZIP 文件。

还有一个值得强调的细节：ZIP 包里不一定非得是游戏。

它可以是 DOS 工具、文本界面应用，或者几乎任何兼容的 DOS 程序。

无需申请多余的存储权限。通过 Android 系统文件选择器，应用只访问你主动选择的文件。

一个叫 STARFALL 的小游戏​

我们还用汇编语言开发了一款非常小巧的 16 位 DOS 街机游戏。

大约 5 KB。一个 COM 可执行文件。不需要运行时环境，也没有任何外部依赖库。

它涵盖了 VGA 图形显示、BIOS 键盘输入和 PC Speaker 蜂鸣器音频。

有时候，证明一个完整模拟器能够正常工作的最好方式，就是准备一个比社交媒体头像还小的游戏。😂

而对于开发者来说，还有另一段故事​

我们不想只交付一个 APK，然后把所有实现细节都藏起来。

项目同时提供：

  • 可复现的 Android NDK/CMake 构建流程。
  • 用于开发和测试的 Linux 桌面基准环境。
  • CPU 核心性能基准测试工具。
  • 无 Root 开发工具链 —— 不需要 root，也不需要 sudo。
  • 移植说明、性能测试文档，以及完整的源代码。
  • GNU GPL-2.0 开源协议，延续 DOSBox 的开源传承。

Android 平台相关的修改尽可能保持精简和局部化，让上游 DOSBox 的核心实现尽可能保持原貌。

整个实现都写在一处地方 —— 那份技术参考文档 —— 配着图表、源码引用和实测数据。

为什么要做这个项目？​

技术一直在进步，但这不应该意味着过去的一切都变得无法访问。

还有成千上万款经典 DOS 游戏、教育软件、商业工具和各种应用程序，值得继续被使用、被发现、被保存。

我们认为，数字遗产保护不应该只局限于博物馆、虚拟机或者复古硬件收藏爱好者。

有时候，保护经典其实很简单：让旧的东西能够在新的设备上继续运行。

现在，你口袋里的手机也可以打开一个 DOS 命令提示符。

而某个 90 年代的计算机爱好者，可能正在疑惑：为什么运行一个 5 KB 的游戏，竟然需要 8 个 CPU 核心？😁

这是一个里程碑，不是终点​

安卓移植阶段已经完成，这个项目带上了一个标注它的标签：

milestone/android-migration-complete

模拟器核心能为三个 ABI 编译，应用层在真机上跑得动，存档能装下整台机器——包括声音芯片——桌面基线也能正常链接。接下来进入维护阶段：修 bug、打磨文档，不再增加新功能。

拿去用​

WhereQ-DOSBox 是一个开源项目，而这段旅程还在继续。

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox

如果你也曾经经历过 DOS 时代，我们很想听听你的想法：

如果可以让一款经典 DOS 游戏或应用重新焕发生命，你最想让哪一个回来？

即使那些老电脑早已不在，也让它们曾经创造的精彩继续运行下去。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

你口袋里的手机能打开一个 DOS 提示符。整个想法就是这一句话，只是做出来比应该花的时间更久。如果你记得某个值得再跑一次的 DOS 程序，告诉我们是哪一个 —— 也许我们会把它做出来。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox: Yesterday's Computing. Today's Pocket. Tomorrow's Possibilities.
entry.content:
Remember when computers had no app stores, no touchscreens, no cloud accounts, and somehow we still managed to spend entire weekends playing games? 😂

We used to type commands like C:\GAMES\DOOM.EXE and consider ourselves computer experts.

Well, DOS never really left. It was just waiting for a smaller computer.

Today, we're taking a meaningful step in bringing that world to Android with WhereQ-DOSBox.

Not a DOS emulator running inside a browser. Not a remote desktop connecting to an old PC. It's a native Android application with the actual DOSBox emulator core running as a native library inside the APK.

And there's quite a bit more behind it.

Watch it running​

WhereQ-DOSBox on a phone: FIFA 96 in the middle, the two console pads in the letterbox bars either side, and the 1990 World Cup song under it. Everything on screen is the real DOSBox core, running as a native library inside the APK.

More than just running DOS games​

Native Android architecture​

DOSBox r4305 with SDL2, integrated through Android NDK and CMake. Native execution across ARM64, ARMv7 and x86_64.

Intelligent CPU execution​

The core=auto configuration automatically uses the interpreter for real-mode applications and switches to dynamic recompilation (JIT) for protected-mode applications. DOS/4GW programs are part of the compatibility journey.

A keyboard that understands mobile​

DOS games were designed for keyboards, not thumbs. We didn't simply shrink a desktop keyboard onto a phone.

The 4:3 DOS display stays in the middle, while frequently used controls occupy the left and right letterbox areas in landscape mode. Portrait mode gets a compact bottom keyboard.

Your DOS environment, your programs​

Import ZIP bundles, install multiple bundles from a folder, or open ZIP files directly from Android's file manager.

And here's an important distinction: a bundle doesn't have to contain a game. It can be a DOS utility, a text-mode application, or practically any compatible DOS program.

No unnecessary storage permissions. Android's system file picker provides access only to the files you select.

A little game called STARFALL​

We also built a tiny 16-bit DOS arcade game in assembly.

Approximately 5 KB. One COM executable. No runtime. No external libraries.

It exercises VGA graphics, BIOS keyboard input and PC speaker audio.

Sometimes the best way to demonstrate an entire emulator is with a game smaller than the average social media profile picture. 😂

And for developers, there's another story​

We didn't want to deliver just an APK and hide everything else.

The project includes:

  • A reproducible NDK/CMake Android build.
  • A desktop Linux baseline for development and testing.
  • CPU-core benchmarking tools.
  • A rootless development toolchain — no root, no sudo required.
  • Porting notes and benchmark documentation, plus the complete source code.
  • GNU GPL-2.0 licensing, preserving the open-source lineage of DOSBox.

The Android-specific changes are kept relatively small and localized, leaving the upstream DOSBox implementation largely intact.

The whole implementation is written up in one place — the technical reference — with the diagrams, the source references and the measured numbers.

Why build this?​

Technology moves forward, but that shouldn't mean everything behind us becomes inaccessible.

There are thousands of classic DOS games, educational programs, business utilities and pieces of software that deserve to remain usable and discoverable.

We believe preservation shouldn't be limited to museums, virtual machines or vintage hardware collectors.

Sometimes, preservation simply means making something old work on something new.

A phone in your pocket can now open a DOS prompt.

And somewhere, a 1990s computer enthusiast is probably wondering why we need 8 CPU cores to run a 5 KB game. 😁

A milestone, not an ending​

The Android migration is finished, and the project carries a tag that says so:

milestone/android-migration-complete

The emulator core builds for three ABIs, the app layer works on a real device, save states carry the whole machine — the sound chips included — and the desktop baseline links. What comes next is maintenance: bug fixes and documentation polish, no new features.

Get it​

WhereQ-DOSBox is open source, and the journey is ongoing.

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox

If you grew up with DOS, we'd love to hear from you:

What's the one DOS application or game you would bring back to life first?

Let's keep the old machines running, even when the machines themselves are no longer around.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

A phone in your pocket can open a DOS prompt. That is the whole idea, and it took longer than it should have. If you remember a DOS program that deserves another run, tell us which one — we might build it.

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.8：保存整台机器，让「继续」真的能继续
entry.content:
一个会骗人的按钮​

两个版本之前，我给启动器加了一个 Resume 按钮。它看上去就是个承诺：按一下，回到你刚才在玩的那局游戏。

结果不是。它每次都把上一款游戏从头开始。

我自己一直没发现，因为我桌上的模拟器进程还活着——游戏其实从没停过，自然也就没什么好「恢复」的。后来有位用户在手机上按了那个按钮，丢掉了一个小时的进度，直截了当地告诉我：你这个 Resume 其实是重开。

他没说错。而修它并不是改一行代码就行的——要做的是给整台机器拍一张快照。

认真做的话，存档是什么​

DOS 游戏自己通常有存档。有的游戏有，很多没有；有的只把进度写在当前目录里，然后指望你自己找到菜单走回去。

存档点（save state）是另一回事：它是被冻住的整台机器。

不是游戏，而是机器。带着寄存器的 CPU、DOS 内存、显存、硬件定时器，以及程序当时正打开的那些文件。是所有让这一局成为「此刻这一局」的东西——所以读档回来是回到同一个瞬间，而不是回到附近。

DOSBox r4305 本身没有存档点，所以我在这个移植里写了一个。每个游戏有 三个槽位，以文件形式存在应用的私有目录里，因此退出应用、重启手机、升级 APK 都丢不掉。

每个游戏三个槽位。Save 冻住正在运行的机器，Load 把它放回去。槽位是手机 上的文件，退出应用也不会丢。

这里有个细节我啃了两天，值得写下来，因为它是「存档能用」和「存档会把游戏搞崩」的分界线。

快照必须在安全点上拍：客机程序得真的在跑，画面得已经稳定，而且 CPU 不能正站在一个挂着 IRET 的中断回调里。位置选错了，读档就会落进 BIOS 调用的半截里——那种损坏看起来像游戏坏了，而不是像存档坏了。

而且它必须把 DOS 层一起拍下来，不只是 CPU。开着 SOUND\MUSIC.FLX 的游戏，指望回来时那个文件还开着。不把文件句柄放进快照，Ultima VIII 每次读档后一秒左右就会走进自己的 extender，然后以 DOS Error=0006 (invalid handle) 中止。放进去之后，那十六个句柄都回来了，音乐也还在响。

于是「继续」终于真的是继续​

这个按钮现在会读回你上次玩的那个游戏的最新槽位，而且会告诉你它要干什么：Resume whereq-demo-bundle · slot 1 · just now。如果一个槽位都没存，它就照旧从头开始。

Saved to slot 1——Resume 按钮已经知道了一切：哪个游戏、哪个槽位、多久之前 存的。

这不是一个「复制文件」的按钮。应用会先把自己的进程拆掉，干净地启动一个什么都没排队的模拟器，等画面稳定下来，然后才把机器恢复进去。早了那么一瞬间——比如手机还在转屏——就会恢复进一个马上就要被丢弃的渲染器里，屏幕一片黑。这条我也追了一阵。

说不清楚的那部分​

有些老 DOS 程序确实过不了读档这一关。 Ultima VIII 的 extender 仍然会在读档后一秒左右中止：Exit to error: RET from illegal descriptor type 13。

这不是应用的问题，也不是「继续」这条路的问题：手动打开面板读同一个槽位，结果完全一样。快照目前还没装下的，是 DOS/4GW 游戏真正依赖的那部分宿主状态——声卡和它的 DMA、EMS 与 XMS 的句柄表、VCPI 的 PIC 向量重映射、鼠标、RTC，以及 PIC 的事件队列。这是还没做完的里程碑，移植日志里写的也是同样的话。

在那之前：STARFALL 存读都完全正常；Ultima VIII 这类游戏可以存、可以读，但它的 extender 读到之后不太高兴。

游戏现在也能在后台活着了​

另一件我原本想当然的事，是以为离开应用就等于离开游戏。Android 上不是这样：系统随时可以回收一个后台应用的进程，而 DOSBox 把整台机器都放在内存里——于是游戏就那么没了，连个提示都没有。

现在只要游戏在跑，就有一条常驻通知把进程保住。切到别的应用去，晚点再回来，游戏还在你离开的那一帧——不用存档，不用重载。

手机上的实际画面。四个方向键现在是真键盘上的倒 T 形——上键在最上面，左右并排， 下键在最下面——手指靠形状就能找对方向。

最后这条改动很小，但我挺喜欢。方向键原本是一根竖排的队列，这和它要代替的那块键盘完全不像：手指必须先「知道」四个键分别是哪一个。现在拇指直接读形状就行。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 就在仓库里，用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装 1.0.0.7：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.8

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk
sha256: ed17f39bddeb9e871485df390f772f19c5a43abdbf3b5845c7abd4afbb602ca3

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：构建指南、移植日志（里面有一节专门讲快照到底怎么拍的，以及为什么必须等安全点）、性能测试笔记，以及这个移植的每一行代码。请去读那些，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

如果你按下「继续」，游戏真的回到了离开时的样子——或者没有，而存档点正是你放弃的地方——请告诉我。我一直在记一份名单，那是最有用的一种反馈。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.8: save the whole machine, and a Resume button that resumes
entry.content:
The button that lied​

Two releases ago I gave the launcher a Resume button. It looked like a promise: press it, and you are back in the game you were playing.

It was not. It started the last game from the beginning, every time.

I did not notice it myself, because on my desk the emulator process was still alive — the game had never really stopped, so there was nothing to resume. Then somebody on a phone pressed the button, lost an hour of progress, and told me plainly: the Resume button restarts the game.

They were right, and the fix was not a one-liner. It took a whole-machine snapshot.

What a save state is, when you are serious about it​

A DOS game has its own save files. Some games have them; many do not; the ones that do usually save somewhere in the current directory and expect you to find your way back through a menu.

A save state is a different thing: it is the entire machine, frozen.

Not the game — the machine. The CPU with its registers, the DOS memory, the video memory, the hardware timers, the files the program had open. Everything that made the game that game at that moment, so that restoring it puts you back in the same instant rather than near it.

DOSBox r4305 has no save state at all, so I wrote one into the port. Every game gets three slots, written as files in the app's private directory, which means they survive quitting the app, rebooting the phone, and updating the APK.

Three slots per game. Save freezes the running machine, Load puts it back. The slots are files on the phone — they survive quitting the app.

There is a subtlety that cost me two days and is worth writing down, because it is the difference between a snapshot that works and one that crashes the game.

The snapshot has to be taken at a safe point: the guest program must actually be running, the picture must have settled, and the CPU must not be standing inside an interrupt callback with an IRET pending. Take it in the wrong place and you restore into the middle of a BIOS call — the kind of corruption that looks like a broken game rather than a broken save.

And it has to capture the DOS layer, not just the CPU. A game that has SOUND\MUSIC.FLX open expects that file to still be open when it comes back. Without the file handles in the snapshot, Ultima VIII walked into its own extender and aborted with DOS Error=0006 (invalid handle) a second after every restore. With them, the sixteen handles come back and the music keeps playing.

So now Resume means resume​

The button restores the newest slot of the last game you played, and it tells you what it is about to do: Resume whereq-demo-bundle · slot 1 · just now. With no slot saved, it starts the game from the beginning, exactly as before.

Saved to slot 1 — and the Resume button already knows: the game, the slot, and how long ago it was written.

Under the hood this is not a button that copies a file. The app tears its own process down, boots a clean emulator with nothing queued, waits for the picture to settle, and only then restores the machine into it. A restore that happens a fraction of a second too early — while the phone is still rotating the screen — restores into a renderer that is about to be thrown away, and you get a black screen. I chased that one for a while too.

The honest part​

Some old DOS programs do not survive a restore. Ultima VIII's extender still aborts about a second after the load, with Exit to error: RET from illegal descriptor type 13.

That is not the app, and it is not the Resume path: loading the same slot by hand, with the panel open, does exactly the same thing. What the snapshot does not capture yet is the rest of the host state a DOS/4GW game leans on — the sound chips and their DMA, the EMS and XMS handle tables, the VCPI PIC vector remapping, the mouse, the RTC, and the PIC event queue. It is milestone work that is not finished, and the porting log says so in the same words.

Until it is: STARFALL saves and resumes perfectly, and a game like Ultima VIII can be saved and restored, but its extender does not like what it finds.

The game keeps running now, too​

The other thing I got wrong was assuming that leaving the app would leave the game alone. On Android it does not: the OS is free to reclaim the process of a backgrounded app, and DOSBox keeps the whole machine in RAM — so the game was simply gone, with no warning.

While a game is running, a small ongoing notification now holds the process. Switch to another app, come back later, and the game is exactly where you left it — no save, no reload, just the frame you walked away from.

The app on a phone. The four arrows now sit in the inverted T of a real keyboard — up on top, left and right side by side, down below — so the thumb finds the direction by shape alone.

That last change is small and I am fond of it. The arrows used to be a single vertical column, which is nothing like the keyboard they stand in for: the finger had to know which of the four was which. Now the thumb reads the shape.

Get it​

The release APK is in the repository, signed with the release key, so it installs over 1.0.0.7 in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.8

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.8.apk
sha256: ed17f39bddeb9e871485df390f772f19c5a43abdbf3b5845c7abd4afbb602ca3

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the build guide, the porting log — including the section that explains exactly how a snapshot is taken and why it has to wait for a safe point — the benchmark notes, and every line of the port. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If you press Resume and your game comes back exactly where you left it — or if it does not, and the save state is where you give up on it — tell me. I am keeping a list, and it is the most useful thing anyone can send me.

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.9：把键盘改造成掌机
entry.content:
一个戴着键盘外形的妥协​

DOS 的画面是 4:3，手机横过来是 20:9。多出来的那部分就是左右两条黑边，前两个版本里，键盘就住在那两条黑边上。

那两条黑边并不算糟。方向键排成真键盘上的倒 T 形，修饰键和编辑键在另一侧，画面占住了整个屏幕中间。用起来是没问题的。

但对一个想模拟的东西来说，那是错的形状。DOS 游戏是左手拇指管方向、右手拇指管按键的，而这些键全都不在拇指习惯待的地方。

掌机是怎么做的​

掌机的做法是：屏幕放中间，操作键分到两只手上——一边一个——而且绝不让按键盖到画面上。

1.0.0.9 就是照着这个来的。那两条黑边不再是「能塞多少塞多少」的两列键，而是两块手柄区，画面依然完整地留在中间。

左手那半负责方向键和左半边键盘，右手那半负责动作键和右半边。画面留在中间， 没有一个键画在它上面。

左半边是负责转向的那只手：四个方向键做成十字键——上键在最上面，左右并排，下键在最下面，手指靠形状就能读出方向——再往上是劈成两半的 QWERTY 的左半边，最顶上一排是 File、Esc 和 Tab。

右半边是负责操作的那只手：拇指下面是 Alt、Ctrl、Shift、Space 和 Enter，往上是 QWERTY 的右半边，最顶上一排是 #+=、Fn 和退格。

QWERTY 是「劈开」的，不是「缩小」的。左边是 12345 qwert asdfg zxcvb，右边是 67890 yuiop hjkl: nm./\——每一半都是正常尺寸的真键，而不是把整块键盘缩小后的玩具。

三层，一个键一层​

键盘劈成两半只解决了一半问题；另一半是键不够用的时候怎么办。这里的答案是一层一个键，就放在右半边最上面那一排。

#+= 把两半同时换成标点。切到这一层时，这个键会亮成蓝色，并且变成 abc——因为按下它就是回到字母层。

标点层。每个带 Shift 的字符就在它对应的不带 Shift 的键正下方，被切走的那个键会亮起来。

Fn 换来功能键：左边是 F1 到 F12，右边是 Ins / Del、Home / End、PgUp / PgDn、Caps、PrtSc 和 Pause。

功能层——整个 F 排和编辑键，一个字母键都不用让出来。

而右半边的字母层本身就已经带着 : . / \，所以敲一条 DOS 路径根本不需要切层：C:\GAMES\DUNE\SETUP.EXE 只是一串字母加标点，在同一层上顺序按下去就行。

Ctrl、Alt 和 Shift，按游戏想要的方式来​

修饰键是我想得最久的一部分，因为两种游戏对 Ctrl 的要求是不一样的。

点一下 Ctrl、Alt 或 Shift 会让它待命：接下来按的那个键会被修饰，然后修饰键自己松开。Ctrl、然后 C——文本编辑器和 DOS 命令行要的就是这个。

按住则是一直按着，直到你松手，和真键盘一样。这正是游戏对开火键和移动键的期待：右拇指按住 Ctrl，左拇指在十字键上走，游戏两个都收得到。

旧键盘只能做前一种。新的手柄区两种都能做，因为修饰键无非就是一个「处于按下状态」的键。

布局跟着屏幕走​

不是每部手机都能腾出 20:9 那么宽的黑边，所以键盘会按黑边的宽度挑自己的形态：宽度够（至少 116 dp）就用完整的两块手柄区，差一点就退回到每侧一列键加上可折叠的 QWERTY 面板，竖屏则是贴底边的一条窄条。

下面这部分我并不满意。

同一套布局在 18:9 屏幕上。手柄区照样放得下，但字母键明显小了——大约 24 dp 宽， 而 20:9 屏上是 33 dp。

在 20:9 屏上，字母键的宽度是 32.8 dp。到了 18:9 屏——很多手机就是这个比例——黑边变窄，同一套布局下字母键只剩 23.6 dp，大约是屏幕宽度的 2.9 %，而正常手机键盘的一个键差不多是这个的两倍。十字键和动作键不受影响，挤小的只有字母。

这个数是量出来的，不是我猜的：两种宽度都在模拟器上跑过、也都实际敲过字，三层布局在两种宽度下的截图都在仓库里。我没有做的是在真正的 18:9 手机上试——这台设备上没有的读者如果愿意替我补上这一课，我很想听。

底下什么都没变​

这一版全是应用层的工作。SDL 的 surface 依然是全屏，键盘只画在画面两侧的黑边里，libdosbox.so 和 1.0.0.8 发出来的是同一个库——同样的原生核心，同样的编译参数。

有时候，描述一个大改动最诚实的方式，是说清楚什么没有变。

流水线现在会自己出版本​

这个仓库第一次有了 CI 流水线。每次推送和每个 PR，ci.yml 都会把模拟器从源码编译三个 ABI——SDL2 加整个 DOSBox 核心，编译三遍——再在上面打包出应用，并检查三个原生库确实都进了 APK。

遇到 v* 标签时，release.yml 会编译发布版 APK、用发布密钥签名、比对证书指纹，然后把它连同 SHA-256 一起发成 GitHub Release。

密钥本身放在仓库的 secrets 里——keystore 用 base64 编码，密码和别名放在旁边——绝不进代码库。流水线会拒绝发布证书对不上的构建：换了密钥签出来的 APK 装不上旧版本，而让用户在自己的手机上发现这件事，不是发现的好地方。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 就在仓库里，用发布密钥签名，可以直接覆盖安装 1.0.0.8：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.9

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.9.apk
sha256: cd6d0bdafd0f84c7324936c89a6cab14ed87a21e4211ed8909078b4a7a51ac02

它跑在 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备上，要求 Android 5.0 及以上，完全离线，不需要账号，没有任何追踪。项目采用 GPL-2.0 许可，DOSBox 核心连同它的 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头注释一起嵌入。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：构建指南、移植日志（里面有一节专门讲那三条宽度规则和量出来的键宽）、键盘本身的设计笔记，以及这个移植的每一行代码。请去读那些，而不是信我的一面之词。

谢谢 DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。

这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。

如果你手上的手机屏幕比较窄、觉得字母键太小——请告诉我。这一版里唯一一件我希望在发布前就见到真机的事情，与其我自己发现，不如你来告诉我。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.9: the keyboard becomes a handheld console
entry.content:
A compromise, wearing the shape of a keyboard​

The DOS picture is 4:3. A phone in landscape is 20:9. The difference is two black bars, one on each side of the picture, and for two releases those bars were where the keys lived.

They were not bad bars. The arrows went into the inverted T of a real keyboard, the modifiers and the editing keys into the other side, and the picture kept the whole middle of the screen. It worked.

It was also the wrong shape for the thing it was standing in for. A DOS game is played with the left thumb on the arrows and the right thumb on the keys, and every one of those keys was a long way from where a thumb expects it.

What a handheld console does​

A handheld console puts the screen in the middle and the controls in your hands — one hand on each side — and it never lets the controls sit on top of the picture.

That is the whole idea behind 1.0.0.9. The bars are no longer two columns of whatever fitted; they are two pads, and the picture sits untouched in the middle.

The left pad carries the arrows and the left half of the keyboard, the right pad the action keys and the right half. The picture keeps the middle, and nothing is drawn over it.

The left pad is the thumb that steers: the four arrows as a D-pad — up on top, left and right side by side, down below, so the finger reads the direction by shape alone — and above them the left half of a split QWERTY, with File, Esc and Tab along the top.

The right pad is the thumb that acts: Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Space and Enter under the right thumb, the right half of the QWERTY above them, and #+=, Fn and Backspace along the top.

The QWERTY is split rather than shrunk. 12345 qwert asdfg zxcvb on the left, 67890 yuiop hjkl: nm./\ on the right — each half is a real key size, not a miniature of the whole thing.

Three layers, one key each​

A split keyboard is only half the story; the other half is what you do when you run out of keys. The answer here is one key per layer, in the top row of the right pad.

#+= swaps both halves for the punctuation. The key lights up blue while its layer is on, and turns into abc, because that is what pressing it brings you back to.

The punctuation layer. Every shifted character sits directly below its unshifted key, and the switched key is lit.

Fn brings up the functions: F1 to F12 on the left, and Ins / Del, Home / End, PgUp / PgDn, Caps, PrtSc and Pause on the right.

The function layer — the whole F-row and the editing keys, without stealing a single key from the letters.

And because the letter layer of the right half already carries : . / \, typing a DOS path needs no layer switch at all: C:\GAMES\DUNE\SETUP.EXE is just letters and punctuation, in that order, on one layer.

Ctrl, Alt and Shift, the way a game wants them​

The modifiers were the part I had to think about longest, because two different games want two different things from Ctrl.

A tap on Ctrl, Alt or Shift arms it: the next key you press is modified, and the modifier releases itself. Ctrl, then C — that is what a text editor or a DOS shell wants.

A hold keeps it pressed for as long as your finger is down, like a real key. That is what a game wants from its fire and strafe keys: hold Ctrl on the right thumb while the left thumb walks the D-pad, and the game sees both at once.

The old keyboard could only do the first one. The new pads do both, because a modifier is just a key that is down.

The layout follows the screen​

Not every phone has 20:9 of letterbox to work with, so the keyboard picks its shape from the width of the bar: the full pads when there is room for them (at least 116 dp), a single key column per side with the fold-up QWERTY when there is less, and a slim strip along the bottom in portrait.

Here is the part I am not happy about.

The same layout on an 18:9 screen. The pads still fit, but the letters are small — about 24 dp wide, against 33 dp on a 20:9 screen.

On a 20:9 screen the letter keys come out at 32.8 dp wide. On an 18:9 screen — the shape of a lot of phones — the bars are narrower and the same layout leaves the letters at 23.6 dp, about 2.9 % of the screen width, where a normal phone keyboard key is roughly twice that. The D-pad and the action keys keep their full size; it is the letters that get tight.

I measured it rather than guessed: both widths were run on the emulator and typed into, and the screenshots of all three layers at both widths are in the repository. What I have not done is try it on a physical 18:9 phone, and that is the gap I would want a reader with such a phone to close for me.

Nothing underneath changed​

The whole release is app-layer work. The SDL surface stays full-screen, the keyboard only ever draws in the bars beside the picture, and libdosbox.so is the same library 1.0.0.8 shipped — byte for byte the same native core, recompiled with the same flags.

Sometimes the honest way to describe a big change is to say what did not change.

The pipeline builds the releases now​

The repository has a CI pipeline for the first time. On every push and every pull request, ci.yml builds the emulator from source for all three ABIs — SDL2 and the whole DOSBox core, three times — and packages an app on top of them, checking that all three native libraries really made it into the APK.

On a v* tag, release.yml builds the release APK, signs it with the release key, checks the certificate against the known fingerprint, and publishes it as a GitHub Release with its SHA-256.

The key itself lives in the repository's secrets — the keystore base64-encoded, the store password and the alias beside it — and never in the tree. The pipeline refuses to publish if the certificate is not the one every previous release was signed with, because an APK signed with a different key cannot be installed over the old one, and finding that out on a user's phone is not a good place to find it.

Get it​

The release APK is in the repository, signed with the release key, so it installs over 1.0.0.8 in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.9

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.9.apk
sha256: cd6d0bdafd0f84c7324936c89a6cab14ed87a21e4211ed8909078b4a7a51ac02

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking. The project is GPL-2.0, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the build guide, the porting log — including the section that explains the three width rules and the measured key sizes — the design notes of the keyboard itself, and every line of the port. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If you have a phone with a narrow screen and the letters feel too small — tell me. That is the one thing in this release I would like to have seen on real hardware before shipping it, and I would rather hear it from you than find it out myself.

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.7：跑自己的 DOS 游戏、真正的 JIT，以及一个塞得进手机的启动器
entry.content:
模拟器是最简单的那一环​

昨天，我把 WhereQ-DOSBox 放到了外面——DOSBox 的原生 Android 移植版，模拟器核心以真正的 libdosbox.so 跑在 APK 里面。

那篇发布公告许下了一个愿：你自己的 DOS 游戏，跑在你口袋里那台真正的机器上。

这种愿望，要是只做到“能启动、能看到 C:\> 提示符”，很便宜。可一旦有人真的拿去用，模拟器反而成了整个问题里最小的一块。

所以从 v1.0.0.2 到 v1.0.0.7，这六个版本真正修掉的东西，是这些。

第一件事：游戏怎么进到手机里？​

这是第一道墙。DOSBox 起来了，然后你面对着一个空空的驱动器。你的游戏躺在某个 1997 年的 .zip 里，而手机上的文件管理器不会替你把 DOS 目录树解开。

于是 App 里长出了一个启动器。一个 .zip 就是一个套装（bundle）：任意一个 DOS 程序，解压一次，放进挂载好的 C: 盘的 C:\GAMES\<n>，再配一个把它启动起来的 RUN.BAT。三种进法，一种权限都不用申请：

  • 系统文件选择器，装单个 .zip；
  • 系统文件夹选择器，把一个文件夹里的 .zip 一次性全解开；
  • 以及用 WhereQ-DOSBox 打开——在文件管理器里点一下，套装自己就装好了。

Files 面板。两个套装，点一下就能开玩；还有一个永远有效的逃生通道 （Exit to prompt）——哪怕游戏已经卡死或者黑屏了，它也管用。

有一个细节比看上去费事：DOSBox 是在挂载驱动器的那一刻缓存目录列表的。之后才装进去的套装，不在那份缓存里；于是会去枚举自己文件的安装程序，什么也找不到。所以启动器每开一个游戏，都会让模拟器重启进一个干净的进程、重新挂载一次 C: 盘。多花一秒，但这正是“装上了”和“真的能跑”的区别。

第二件事：那个按钮的名字起错了​

启动器刚来的时候，按钮叫 Games——因为我想当然地以为大家只想要游戏。但那个名字是错的：启动器打开的并不是游戏，而是套装；一个套装可以装着任何 DOS 程序——一个工具、一个文本界面的程序、一个 demo、一集你一直想打完的 shareware。

所以按钮现在叫 File——DOS 时代的老叫法——面板也改成了 Files：Install a bundle (.zip)、No bundles installed yet.、Start file…。

这是件小事。但正是这种小事，把一个演示变成一个工具。

第三件事：键盘塞不进屏幕​

屏幕键盘原本是 21 个等宽的键。横屏的时候，这比手机还宽——最后一个键被切掉，根本按不到。现在这些键改成按权重分配，整条键盘永远正好铺满屏幕宽度。

接着键盘条本身又成了问题：它吃掉了三分之一的屏幕。DOS 画面是 4:3 的，横屏两侧本来就有黑边——于是那些常驻按键现在直接住进了这两条黑边里，变成左右两列。左边是 Ctrl、Alt、Shift 这些修饰键，右边是 File、Ent、Space 和方向键，整块屏幕中间完整地留给 DOS。

示例套装 STARFALL 跑在新布局里：游戏在中间，按键在两侧的黑边里。

更重的一件事：JIT，和那些需要它的游戏​

实模式的 DOS 程序用解释器跑得非常好——DOSBox 本来就是这么写的，对任何 8 位、16 位的程序来说解释器都够快。

保护模式程序是另一回事。DOS/4GW 扩展程序、保护模式游戏：那是一套不同的 CPU 模型，而解释器只能一条指令一条指令地走。Ultima VIII 就是一个 DOS/4GW 保护模式游戏——而保护模式代码，正是重编译核心存在的理由。

DOSBox 自带一个 JIT——重编译核心，在运行时直接生成机器码。上游是靠 GCC 插件来编译它的，而 NDK 的 clang 做不到；Android 又禁止让可写的内存可执行，而原版的代码缓存正是这么干的。

这两个问题最后都有解。可移植的代码生成器（arm64、armv7、x86_64）不需要插件，直接往一块缓冲区里生成机器码；那块缓冲区改用匿名 PROT_EXEC 映射，而不是可写的堆内存，来获得可执行权限。现在这个 JIT 已经编进了三个 Android ABI 的 libdosbox.so。

而随包发布的配置是 core=auto：

  • 一直待在实模式的程序跑解释器，跟以前一模一样——JIT 根本不会启动，代码缓存连分配都不会发生；
  • 一旦切换到保护模式的程序，在第一次模式切换的那一刻交给重编译核心。

欢迎画面和已挂载的 C: 盘，按键在两侧黑边里。中间跑的是货真价实的 DOSBox 核心， 不是一个仿写的实现。

关于 APK 体积，我得说实话​

第一篇公告里说 APK 大约 5.3 MB。现在大约 15.5 MB——与其让你下载时才发现，不如我先解释清楚。

两个原因，都是故意的。原生库在 APK 里是不压缩存放的，这样 Android 可以直接从 APK 里映射它们，而不用每次安装都复制到磁盘——差别的大头在这儿。另外 App 层现在是 Kotlin + AndroidX，带来了大约 4.5 MB 的 dex。

这笔交换是：下载大一点，换来更快的安装，以及一台更像机器的机器。

我写进文档、却没做出来的那个设置​

v1.0.0.6 里，我在文档里、在这个仓库里写过这么一句：“如果 JIT 的代码缓存分配不出来，就把 core=normal 写进 dosbox.conf 作为退路。”

然后我自己照着这句话试了一遍。dosbox.conf 每次启动都会从随包的模板重新生成——这是故意的，这样模板一改，已经装在手机上的版本也能拿到。而这意味着手工改过的 dosbox.conf 会在下次启动时被覆盖。何况那个文件本来就在 App 的私有目录里，任何文件管理器都够不着。

我文档里写的那个退路，其实根本够不着。 确实有那么一小撮老 DOS 程序在重编译核心上会出毛病，而我当时没给它们留任何出路。

所以 Files 面板现在多了一个 Config 按钮：

CPU core 现在可以在 App 里选：Auto（默认）、Normal、Dynamic、Simple、Prefetch。 DOSBox 是启动时决定用哪个核心的，所以 App 会问你要不要重启。

这个选择会被存下来，写进生成出来的配置文件，重启之后还在，App 升级之后也还在。一个小对话框，换来一句终于能兑现的承诺。

还改了什么​

App 层从 Java 换成了 Kotlin——同样的八个类，重写了一遍——Gradle 现在是正式的构建方式。发布脚本学会了更新 Android manifest，也不再把整个工作树一股脑塞进发布提交里。模拟器脚本改用真实 GPU，而不是那个会把屏幕画成碎片的软件光栅器。

还有 STARFALL——那个示例套装——已经进了仓库：一个用 16 位 DOS 汇编写的迷你街机游戏，一个大约 5 KB 的 .COM，没有运行时、没有依赖，并且以可以直接安装的 .zip 形式提交了。它的存在是为了让新用户不用先去找一个游戏，就能把整条流程走一遍：装套装、按 Play、看游戏跑起来。

拿去用​

发布版 APK 就在仓库里，用发布密钥签名，所以后来的版本可以直接覆盖安装：

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox —— tag v1.0.0.7

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk
sha256: 2e97f12f3901acbdc23f62395316df25aa51f4a081d941a950b2d7dfa36910a1

支持 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备，Android 5.0 及以上，全程离线，不要账号，不做任何追踪。

这是一个 GPL-2.0 的项目，DOSBox 核心以 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头部的形式完整嵌入。整个移植只动了核心里寥寥几处——SDL 的视频与触摸路径、鼠标映射、JIT 代码缓存的 Android 分支，还有两处只为消掉编译器警告而做的改动。其余全部是上游代码。

再说一遍：这篇文章不是文档。 文档就是仓库本身——构建指南、移植记录、性能测试报告，以及移植部分的每一行代码。请你自己去读，而不是听我在这儿说。

谢谢，DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 是由 DOSBox 团队 写出来的——一群志愿者，把一个 1994 年的操作系统做到了此后世界上每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费送给每一个想要它的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是叠在他们工作之上的一层薄壳。原创、手艺和慷慨，全部属于他们。

这个移植建立在 Em-DOSBox 之上——Boris Gjenero 用 Emscripten 做的 DOSBox r4305 版本；而 Em-DOSBox 本身，起源于 Ismail Khatib 第一次尝试用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox，后来又搭上了 Alon Zakai 在 Emscripten 上的工作。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。

DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；本移植与 DOSBox 团队无隶属关系，也未获其背书。

如果你自己的某个游戏现在能在手机上跑起来了——或者跑不起来，而你在那个 CPU core 对话框前放弃了——都请告诉我。我一直在记一份清单，那是我收到的最有用的东西。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox 1.0.0.7: your own DOS games, a real JIT, and a launcher that fits on a phone
entry.content:
The emulator was the easy part​

Yesterday I put WhereQ-DOSBox out into the world: a native Android port of DOSBox, the emulator core running as a real libdosbox.so inside an APK.

The announcement made a promise: your own DOS games, on the actual machine in your pocket.

A promise like that is cheap to make with an emulator that boots to a C:\> prompt. It gets expensive the moment someone tries to actually use it — because then the emulator is the smallest part of the problem.

So here is what six releases, v1.0.0.2 through v1.0.0.7, actually fixed.

First: how do you get your games onto the phone?​

This was the wall. DOSBox boots, and then you are staring at a drive with nothing on it. Your games live in a .zip from somewhere in 1997, and the file manager on your phone is not going to unpack a DOS directory tree for you.

So the app grew a launcher. A .zip is a bundle: any DOS program, unpacked once into C:\GAMES\<n> on the mounted C: drive, with a RUN.BAT that starts it. Three ways to get one in, none of which asks for a permission:

  • the system file picker, for a single .zip;
  • the system folder picker, which unpacks every .zip in a folder at once;
  • and Open with WhereQ-DOSBox, so a bundle you tap in a file manager installs itself.

The Files panel. Two bundles, one tap to play, and an escape hatch (Exit to prompt) that always works — even when the game has hung or gone black.

One detail that took more care than it looks: DOSBox caches the directory listing of a drive when it mounts it. A bundle installed afterwards is not in that cache, so an installer that enumerates its own files finds nothing. The launcher therefore restarts the emulator into a clean boot with a freshly mounted C: for every game it starts. It costs a second, and it is the difference between "installed" and "actually runs".

Then: the button was called the wrong thing​

The launcher arrived as a Games button, because that is what I assumed people would want. It was wrong: the launcher does not open games. It opens bundles, and a bundle can hold any DOS program — a utility, a text-mode application, a demo, a shareware episode you always wanted to finish.

So the button is File now — the old DOS way — and the panel is Files. Install a bundle (.zip), No bundles installed yet, Start file…. Small thing. It is the kind of small thing that turns a demo into a tool.

And: the keyboard did not fit on the screen​

The on-screen keyboard had 21 keys of a fixed width. In landscape, that is wider than the phone — the last key was cut off and could not be pressed. The keys are weighed now, so the strip always fills the width exactly.

Then the strip itself became the problem: it ate a third of the screen. The DOS picture is 4:3 and letterboxed, so in landscape there are black bars down the left and right — and the always-on keys now live in those bars as two vertical columns. The modifiers on the left, File, Ent, Space and the arrow keys on the right, and the whole middle of the screen stays a DOS screen.

STARFALL, the example bundle, running in the new layout: the game in the middle, the keys in the bars on either side of it.

The bigger one: a JIT, and the games that needed it​

Real-mode DOS programs run perfectly on an interpreter — DOSBox was written that way, and the interpreter is fast enough for anything 8-bit and 16-bit.

Protected-mode programs are a different story. A DOS/4GW extender, a protected-mode game: that is a different CPU model, and the interpreter walks it instruction by instruction. Ultima VIII — a DOS/4GW game — is exactly the kind of program the recompiler exists for.

DOSBox has a JIT — a recompiling core that emits machine code at run time. Upstream builds it with a GCC plugin, which the NDK's clang cannot do, and Android forbids making writable memory executable, which is what the stock code cache does.

Both problems turned out to be solvable. The portable code generators (arm64, armv7, x86_64) emit machine code into a buffer with no plugin involved, and the buffer is made executable with an anonymous PROT_EXEC mapping instead of a writable heap block. The JIT is now compiled into libdosbox.so for all three Android ABIs.

And the shipped configuration is core=auto:

  • a program that stays in real mode runs on the interpreter, exactly as before — the JIT never engages and the code cache is never even allocated;
  • a program that switches into protected mode hands over to the recompiler at the first mode switch.

The welcome screen and a mounted C: drive, with the keyboard in the bars on either side. The emulator core is the real DOSBox, not a re-implementation of it.

Honest about the APK size​

The first announcement said the APK was about 5.3 MB. It is now about 15.5 MB, and I would rather explain that than let you find out from the download.

Two reasons, both on purpose. The native libraries are stored uncompressed in the APK, so Android can map them straight out of it instead of copying them to disk on every install — that is most of the difference. And the app layer is now Kotlin with AndroidX, which adds roughly 4.5 MB of dex.

The trade is: a bigger download, in exchange for an install that is faster and a machine that behaves like a machine.

The setting I documented but did not ship​

In v1.0.0.6 I wrote, in the documentation and in this very repository: "If the JIT code cache cannot be allocated, put core=normal in dosbox.conf as the fallback."

Then I tried to follow my own advice. dosbox.conf is regenerated from the shipped template on every boot — deliberately, so that a change to the template reaches phones that are already installed. Which means a hand-edited dosbox.conf is overwritten at the next start. And the file lives in the app's private directory anyway, where no file manager can reach it.

The fallback I documented was not reachable. A handful of old DOS programs do misbehave on the recompiler, and I had given them no way out.

So the Files panel has a Config button now:

The CPU core, pickable in the app: Auto (the default), Normal, Dynamic, Simple, Prefetch. DOSBox chooses its core when it starts, so the app asks whether to restart.

The choice is stored and written into the generated configuration, so it survives a restart and an app update. One small dialog — and a promise in the documentation that is now true.

What else changed​

The app layer was ported from Java to Kotlin — the same eight classes, rewritten — and Gradle is now the canonical build. The release script was taught to update the Android manifest, and it no longer stages the whole working tree into a release commit. The emulator script starts the emulator on the real GPU instead of a software rasterizer that drew the screen in scattered tiles.

And STARFALL — the example bundle — is in the tree: a tiny arcade game in 16-bit DOS assembly, one .COM of about 5 KB, no runtime, no libraries, committed as a ready-to-install .zip. It exists so that a new user can see the whole flow — install a bundle, press Play, watch a game run — without having to find a game first.

Get it​

The release APK is in the repository, and it is signed with the release key, so a later version installs over it in place:

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — tag v1.0.0.7

downloads/whereq-dosbox-1.0.0.7.apk
sha256: 2e97f12f3901acbdc23f62395316df25aa51f4a081d941a950b2d7dfa36910a1

It runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices, Android 5.0 and newer, entirely offline, with no account and no tracking.

The project is GPL-2.0 and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact. The port touches the core in only a handful of small, local places — the SDL video and touch paths, the mouse mapping, the Android branch of the JIT's code cache, a couple of fixes that only silence the compiler. Everything else is upstream code.

Again, this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the build guide, the porting log, the benchmark notes, and every line of the port. Please read those rather than take my word for it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input.

DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If a game of yours now runs on your phone — or if it doesn't, and the CPU core dialog is where you give up on it — tell me. I am keeping a list, and it is the most useful thing anyone can send me.

entry.title: 财经今日 开源了：界面、它读的库表结构，以及中间的 API
entry.content:
一个交易日，是六个标签页​

九点二十五，集合竞价结束。九点半，开盘。从这一刻起，接下来四个小时， 市场一直在说话：一次公开市场操作、一个期货点位、一个指数点位、一份征求意见 稿、一份公司公告，再加上一篇分析——而这两者到底差在哪。

这些消息都是真的，也都真实存在。只是它们不在同一个地方。

于是你打开六个标签页：行情快讯、指数页面、板块热力图、日历、公告检索、还有 一个论坛。它们各自的版式、配色、关注点都不一样，而且大多是为别人的问题而 做的。

我一直想要的是一块板子。一屏之内，热榜、7×24 快讯、板块热力、经济日历、个股 热榜同时都在；而且每个面板回答的都是同一个问题：发生了什么变化，有多重要。

财经今日（CaiJing Today） 就是这块板子。它以中文为默认界面，因为市场先说 中文；英文放在旁边，一键可切。

这块板子​

这是运行中的站点——caijing.today——里面是真实数据。左侧是热榜 TOP 50，配 1 小时 / 24 小时 / 本周 / 本月四档时间窗和热度条；中间是编辑精选、 行情图表和个股热榜；右侧是 7×24 快讯、经济日历和全球市场行情；顶部那条是滚动的 行情带。

打开它，版式是刻意做密的。顶部一条行情带横向滚动。往下是三栏面板，每一个都是 同一套数据库的一个切面，谁也不替谁做总结。

  • 热榜 / TOP 50 —— 按热度排序的新闻，右侧可切换时间窗。这里的热度不是编辑 判断，而是由发布时间、该条所挂分析的可信度，以及情绪强度共同算出来的。
  • 7×24 快讯 —— 快讯流。短、带时间戳，有自己的节奏；你读一篇五分钟前打开 的稿子，它也还在旁边走着。
  • 个股热榜 —— 个股热榜，自带一套排序。
  • 分类导航 —— 十二个分类：宏观、股市、美股、债券、外汇、大宗商品、加密、 房产、科技、公司、政策、观点。这不是手工维护的分类表——每一条内容是按它的 信号类型、板块、地域和标签归类的，你也可以手动改。
  • 经济日历 —— 当天的预定数据发布，带重要度。
  • 数据图表 / 行业板块 / 加密市场 / 热搜关键词 —— 走势图、带资金流的板块 热力、加密板块，以及大家正在搜什么。

整套界面两种语言，切换按钮在页头。中文不是英文的翻译——中文才是最初的版式， 英文是后来并排加上去的。

同一块板子的浅色主题。板子默认是深色的，页头的切换按钮可以换，切换结果会 被记住。

技术说明​

  • 前端 —— React 19、TypeScript、Vite、TanStack Query、i18next。类型严格， 55 个测试。
  • 后端 —— FastAPI、SQLAlchemy 2（asyncpg 异步驱动）、Pydantic。 只读：这个服务从不写入它所读的数据库。
  • 数据库 —— PostgreSQL 17。15 张表、2 个视图，以 docs/SCHEMA.sql 的形式公开。
  • API —— /api/v1 下 17 个接口，全部是读。
  • 许可 —— MIT，覆盖整个仓库。
  • 测试 —— 后端 25 个、前端 55 个，CI 里四道关：后端测试、一道把库表契约 真正灌进 PostgreSQL 并和 ORM 映射对账的 schema 检查、前端测试，以及四个镜像 的 Docker 构建。

这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：库表契约、安装指南、数据来源的规矩、 测试矩阵。我更希望你直接去读那些，而不是听我一面之词。

👉 github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today

跑起来：

git clone https://github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today.git
cd CaiJing-Today

cp docker/.env.example docker/.env
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build

然后打开 http://localhost:8080。这就是完整的一栈——PostgreSQL 17、库表契约、 演示数据、API 和前端。API 在 http://localhost:8000，交互式文档在 /docs。

构建、测试、运行都不需要任何 key。 docker/.env.example 里的默认值是本地 开发用的凭据，不是密钥；而且不需要身份提供者：浏览是公开的，所以界面停在匿名 模式，登录入口自动隐藏。

为什么现在把它放出来​

因为采集器是那部分不开源的，而库表结构是开源的。

这个仓库把库表结构当作一份明确的契约公开——15 张表、2 个视图，列的类型、唯一 约束、快照的纪律、时间的 UTC 规矩——再加上一个只读它的 FastAPI 服务。生产环境 里往这些表里灌数据的采集器是另一个组件。

我觉得这个切分才是有用的地方。库表结构不是谁家数据库的导出物，它是两个允许 由不同的人写的程序之间的约定。如果你想要自己的采集器——自己的信源、自己的节 奏、自己对「一条新闻」的理解——那就写一个往这些表里插入的组件，API 和界面不 改一行代码就会把它伺服出来。

这就是全部的扩展点，规矩写在 docs/data-sources.md里： published_at 是什么时区、为什么快照表要新增一个 as_of 而不是更新、哪些分 类 id 是合法的、热度分数由什么构成。

有一句必须说清楚的话。 MIT 许可覆盖的是代码，它对往数据库里放的数据只 字未提。采集器取回来的标题、行情和公告，权利属于发布它们的那家机构，各有各的 条款；财经通讯社、免费公开数据门户和行情数据商给的授权根本不是一回事。你要是 接了真实数据，守约是你的事，不是这个项目的。

还有关于演示数据，说白了：里面每一行都是编的。标题带【示例】/ [sample] 前缀， 价格是假的，日历条目是占位的，链接用的是保留域名 .invalid，热榜里的代码是 DEMO-001 … DEMO-010 而不是真实股票代码。这是有意的——真实代码配一个编出来 的热度，读起来就成了投资建议。

这就是一份全新 checkout 跑起来的样子：同一块板子，跑在合成演示数据上。每条 标题都标着【示例】，代码全是 DEMO-001 … DEMO-010，里面没有一个数字是真的。 界面和线上一样，默认中文。

致谢​

这个应用站在别人的劳动之上，装作不是那样才是不诚实的。

  • Polygon.io —— 行情数据。行情带、指数点位、走势图都 来自它。
  • GDELT —— 全球新闻索引，对应 gdelt 这个 信源 id。
  • SEC EDGAR —— 美国公告索引，对应 sec_edgar 这个信源 id。
  • 东方财富 —— 界面上标注为 akshare_em_global 和 akshare_em_cjzc 的全球 快讯与财经早餐信源。
  • 财经 RSS 聚合 —— rss 这个信源 id 背后的财经 RSS 信息源。
  • React、Vite、 TanStack Query、 i18next、 FastAPI、 SQLAlchemy、 Pydantic、 PostgreSQL、 nginx 和 Docker —— 这个 仓库所依赖的技术栈。依赖清单在 NOTICE 里。

演示数据集则不归任何人所有——这恰恰是它的意义：它是合成的，它自己写明了这一点， 它的存在只是为了让一份全新的 checkout 起来就有东西可看。

如果你照着这份契约写了一个采集器——或者把它改成一块服务于别的市场的板子—— 我很想听听。

entry.title: CaiJing Today is open source — the board, the schema it reads, and the API in between
entry.content:
A market day is a lot of tabs​

At 09:25 the call auction ends. At 09:30 the tape starts, and for the next four hours the Chinese market talks continuously — a central-bank operation, a futures point, an index level, a draft regulation, a company filing, an analyst note about the difference between two of them.

All of it is real, and all of it is somewhere. But it is not in the same place.

So you end up with six tabs open — a wire service, a quote page, a sector heatmap, a calendar, a filing index, a forum — and the tab bar quietly becomes the product. Every one of them is a different layout, a different colour scheme, a different idea of what matters, and most of them are built for somebody else's question.

I kept wanting a single board. One page where the hot list, the 7×24 newsflash, sector heat, the economic calendar and the individual-stock hot list are all visible at once, and where every panel answers the same question: what changed, and how much does it matter?

财经今日 (CaiJing Today) is that board. It is Chinese-first, because that is the language the market speaks first, with English one click away.

The board​

This is the running site — caijing.today — with live data. On the left the TOP 50 hot ranking with its 1-hour / 24-hour / week / month windows and heat bars. In the middle the editorial picks, the market charts and the individual-stock hot list. On the right the 7×24 newsflash, the economic calendar and the global market quotes. The strip across the top scrolls the live quote tape.

Open it and the shape is deliberately dense. A quote strip scrolls along the top. Below that, three columns of panels, each one a window onto the same database, none of them a summary of the others.

  • Hot Ranking (热榜 / TOP 50) — headlines ranked by heat, with a window selector. The heat score is not editorial judgement; it is computed from publication time, the confidence of the analysis attached to the item, and how strong its sentiment is.
  • Live Newsflash (7×24 快讯) — the newsflash. Short, timestamped, and it keeps its own rhythm while you read, so an article you opened five minutes ago still has the tape beside it.
  • Hot Stocks (个股热榜) — the individual-stock hot list, with its own ranking.
  • Categories (分类导航) — twelve categories: 宏观, 股市, 美股, 债券, 外汇, 大宗商品, 加密, 房产, 科技, 公司, 政策, 观点. They are not a hand-made taxonomy — each item is classified from its signal type, sectors, region and tags, and you can disagree with the result by hand.
  • Economic Calendar (经济日历) — the day's scheduled releases, with an importance rating.
  • Market Data / Trending / Global Markets (数据图表 / 热搜关键词 / 全球市场) — the index sparklines, the trending keywords, and the global quote board.
  • Sector Heat / Crypto Market (行业板块 / 加密市场) — the sector heatmap with capital inflow, and the crypto board with coins, chains and TVL.

And the whole thing is in two languages, with the toggle in the header. The Chinese is not a translation of the English — the Chinese is the original layout, and English was added beside it.

The same board in the light theme. The board is dark by default; the toggle in the header switches it, and the choice is remembered.

The honest technical note​

  • Frontend — React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, i18next. Strict types, and 55 tests.
  • Backend — FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 over asyncpg, Pydantic. Read-only: the service never writes to the database it reads.
  • Database — PostgreSQL 17. Fifteen tables and two views, published as docs/SCHEMA.sql.
  • API — seventeen endpoints under /api/v1, all of them reads.
  • Licence — MIT, for the whole repository.
  • Tests — 25 backend, 55 frontend, and four CI gates: the backend suite, a schema job that applies the contract to a real PostgreSQL and checks the ORM mirror against it, the frontend suite, and a Docker build of all four images.

This post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the schema contract, the setup guide, the data-source rules and the test matrix. I would rather you read those than take my word for it.

👉 github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today

To run it:

git clone https://github.com/whereq/CaiJing-Today.git
cd CaiJing-Today

cp docker/.env.example docker/.env
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build

Then open http://localhost:8080. That is the whole stack — PostgreSQL 17, the schema contract, the demo data, the API and the frontend. The API is on http://localhost:8000, with interactive documentation at /docs.

You do not need any keys to build, test or run it. The defaults in docker/.env.example are local development credentials, not secrets, and the site works with no identity provider at all: browsing is public, so the UI stays in anonymous mode and the sign-in control is hidden.

Why it is in the world now​

Because the collector is the part that is not open, and the schema is the part that is.

This repository ships the schema as an explicit contract — 15 tables, two views, the column types, the unique constraints, the snapshot discipline, the UTC rules — and a FastAPI service that reads it and nothing else. The collector that fills those tables in production is a separate component.

I think that split is the useful bit. The schema is not a dump of somebody else's database; it is the agreement between two programs that are allowed to be written by different people. If you want your own collector — your own sources, your own cadence, your own idea of what a headline is — you write a component that inserts into those tables, and the API and the interface serve it with no code changes.

That is the whole extension point, and it is documented in docs/data-sources.md: what published_at means, why the snapshot tables take a new as_of instead of an update, which category ids are legal, and what the heat score is made of.

One warning, because it matters. The MIT licence covers the code. It says nothing about the data you put into the database. The headlines, quotes and filings a collector retrieves belong to the organisations that published them, each under its own terms, and a financial wire, a free public-data portal and a market-data vendor do not grant the same rights. If you connect real data, complying with those terms is your job, not this project's.

And to be plain about the demo dataset: every row in it is invented. The headlines are prefixed 【示例】 / [sample], the prices are fabricated, the calendar entries are placeholders, the links use the reserved .invalid TLD, and the hot-stock list uses DEMO-001 … DEMO-010 rather than real tickers. That is deliberate. A real ticker next to a fabricated heat score reads as investment advice.

This is what a fresh checkout gives you: the same board, running on the synthetic demo dataset. Every headline is marked 【示例】, every ticker reads DEMO-001 … DEMO-010, and nothing in it is real. The interface is Chinese-first, as it is on the live site.

Credits​

This app stands on the work of other people, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise.

  • Polygon.io — market data. The quote strip, the index levels, the charts.
  • GDELT — the global news index behind the gdelt source id.
  • SEC EDGAR — the US filing index behind the sec_edgar source id.
  • 东方财富 (Eastmoney) — the 全球快讯 and 财经早餐 feeds the interface credits as akshare_em_global and akshare_em_cjzc.
  • 财经 RSS 聚合 — the finance RSS feeds behind the rss source id.
  • React, Vite, TanStack Query, i18next, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, nginx and Docker — the stack this repository is built on. The dependency list is in NOTICE.

The demo dataset is also the work of nobody in particular, which is exactly the point: it is synthetic, it says so, and it exists so that a fresh checkout has something to show.

If you write a collector against the schema — or fork the board for a market this one does not cover — I would genuinely like to hear about it.

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox：把 DOS 年代带回手机
entry.content:
角落里那台机器​

我记得的，是风扇的声音。

不是游戏，不是跟软驱较劲的那几个晚上——是风扇。一台米色的主机蹲在父母客厅的角落，风扇转起来像是它正在想什么事情；旁边是一台带点偏绿、微微凸起的 CRT 显示器，那在当时，已经是一扇窗。

那台机器开着的时候，整个房间的温度都不一样。它是家里最吵的东西，而它属于我。

然后，是那个闪烁的光标。

C:\>

这个提示符像是一句邀请。它不自作解释，它只是等着。如果你愿意学它的语言——cd、dir、copy、mkdir——它就会老老实实照你说的做。那是我第一次觉得，电脑是一件工具，而不只是一个用来消费的家电。

游戏，以及游戏底下的软件​

我玩过的那批游戏，现在说来都算经典了：Wolfenstein 3D，软盘被磁头刮花到根本读不出来，我用的是一张有划痕的；Commander Keen，一座明显是两个喝多了咖啡的人做的城市；凌晨两点跟朋友用拨号线路联机打 Liero；Prince of Persia，它教会我必须经常存档，因为我会死很多次；还有 Duke Nukem 和初代 Doom，以及 shareware 那种特定的魔力——这一集恰好断在你知道下一集会从哪里开始的地方。

但真正改变我人生的，其实不是这些游戏，而是游戏周围的软件——以及"它们不过就是磁盘上的文件"这件事。

我写了人生第一个 .BAT 文件。我敲了一条长到需要换行的命令，于是不得不去学"行连接符"。我用文本编辑器打开一个配置文件，改了一行，然后程序的行为就变了。我见过蓝屏，也因此明白：电脑是会坏的；坏是有原因的；我可以去找出那个原因。

然后——那个把我的人生彻底拐向另一个方向、也正是我整个职业生涯起点的瞬间——我意识到：程序不是魔法，它就是文本。

我可以打开它、读它、改它、弄坏它，然后重新把它拼回来。

Turbo Pascal、BASIC、AUTOEXEC.BAT、CONFIG.SYS——它们看起来都是同一个东西换了不同的戏服。那都是某一个人坐下来写下的一串指令，而机器听命了。

这就是启蒙。软件从一个黑盒子，变成了一个你伸得进手去的东西。此后我做的一切——分布式系统、Kubernetes 集群、AI Agent、包括这个网站——都是从那个瞬间长出来的：机器不是一个魔法盒子，它是一台你可以读懂的机器。

然后，整个世界搬进了我们的口袋​

然后，世界有了自己的屏幕。

看看手机变成了什么。它是相机，是钱包，是图书馆，是报纸，是游戏机，是地图，是电话，是银行，是医院，是教室。对今天绝大多数人来说，手机就是那台计算机。阅读、工作、游戏、学习、思考，全都发生在它上面。计算的重心，就这样悄无声息地挪了过来。

这也意味着一件有点可悲的事：那个"数以百万计的人通过命令提示符去驾驭一台机器"的时代，结束了。DOS 年代不只是"旧"——它更是一扇已经关上的门。那一代人第一次真正接触电脑，是从一个闪烁的光标开始的：它问你，你想做什么？而我们这一代，看到的是一堵墙的矩形，永远不必知道底下是什么。

我并不认为这一定更糟。我不是来说"手机不是一台好电脑"的。但我确实觉得，这让我们失去了一些东西。整整一代人对机器的主人感，来自于"你不得不"学会命令行。今天没有人再递给你一个光标了，你拿到的是一屏的应用图标，然后你永远不必知道它们下面是什么。

所以有个问题一直在我脑子里转，简单到有点不好意思问出口：

为什么不把 DOS 带到手机上去？

不是为了做个博物馆展品，不是做一个在网页里跑 demo 的怀旧 App。而是做成一个真的东西——真家伙，在你自己口袋里那台真正的机器上跑，用你自己的 DOS 游戏和软件，就像当年本该有的样子。

WhereQ-DOSBox​

这就是答案。今天，我把它开源了。

欢迎界面、已挂载的驱动器，以及屏幕键盘。触摸就是 DOS 鼠标， 按键直接输入到 DOSBox 里。

WhereQ-DOSBox 是 DOSBox 的原生 Android 移植版——模拟器核心以真正的原生库（libdosbox.so）的形式跑在 APK 里面。不是网页，不是 WebView，不是在 JavaScript 里再模拟一遍 x86。在你的手机上，以原生速度运行。

今天就能做到的事情：

  • 在手机挂载的驱动器上运行你自己的 DOS 软件和游戏。
  • 用屏幕键盘打字——按键直接进 DOSBox。
  • 把触摸屏当成 DOS 鼠标来用。
  • 全程离线，不需要账号，不需要浏览器，也没有任何追踪。

APK 大约 5.3 MB，支持 arm64-v8a、armeabi-v7a 和 x86_64 设备（Android 5.0 及以上）。

它是开源的 —— 请直接去看​

这是一个 GPL-2.0 的项目。DOSBox 核心以 AUTHORS、ChangeLog、COPYING 和逐文件头部完整的形式嵌入进来，完全符合许可证的要求。整个移植只动了核心里的四个地方，都是很小的局部改动；其余全部是上游代码。

有一点我想说得很坦白：这篇文章不是文档。 文档就是仓库本身——构建指南、移植记录、性能测试报告，以及移植部分的每一行代码，全都在公开的地方。我宁愿你自己去读，而不是听我在这儿说。

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox

想自己编译一份：

git clone git@github.com:whereq/whereq-dosbox.git
cd whereq-dosbox
bin/build.sh all      # bootstrap + native + android + apk

跑完，whereq-dosbox-debug.apk 就在 build/apk/ 里。完整指南——包括发布签名、Gradle 那一套、启动图标——都在 BUILDING.md。

我为什么要把它放出来​

因为我一直在遇到这样的人：他们记得 DOS 那个年代，想要它回来——但已经悄悄地接受了"那是不可能的了"，把它跟米色主机、和 3.5 寸软盘一起归档了。

它没有消失。它只是在等一次移植。

如果这能让某个人重新找回一个晚上的一句 C:\>、一个下午的 Commander Keen，或者让一个从来没有过米色主机的小孩第一次体验到"哦——原来是这样运作的"，那这几个月的移植就值了。

如果你也想起了什么，也请一定告诉我。

谢谢，DOSBox​

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。

DOSBox 是由 DOSBox 团队 写出来的——一群志愿者，把一个 1994 年的操作系统做到了世界上此后每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它兼容了大量 DOS 游戏，三十年里一直维护着它，而且这一切都是免费的、送给任何想要的人的。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是叠在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创、手艺和慷慨，全部属于他们。

这个移植建立在 Em-DOSBox 之上——Boris Gjenero 用 Emscripten 做的 DOSBox r4305 版本；而 Em-DOSBox 本身，起源于 Ismail Khatib 第一次尝试用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox，后来又搭上了 Alon Zakai 在 Emscripten 上的工作。他们每一位，都把"DOS 跑在浏览器里"这件事往前推到了当时没人想得到的地方——而正是这个想法，让"DOS 跑在手机上"变得值得一试。

谢谢你们。全部的功劳都属于你们。DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；本移植与 DOSBox 团队无隶属关系，也未获其背书。

如果你还记得某款游戏、某台机器，或者某一个 C:\>——说给我听。我正在把它们收集起来，这会是一份很好的档案。

entry.title: WhereQ-DOSBox: bringing the DOS era back to your phone
entry.content:
The machine in the corner of the room​

I remember the fan first.

Not the games, not the arguments with the diskette drive — the fan. A beige tower in the corner of my parents' living room, its fan whirring like it was thinking about something, and a green-ish CRT screen that was somehow a window. When that machine was on, the whole room changed temperature. It was the loudest thing in the house, and it was mine.

Then came the blinking cursor.

C:\>

That prompt was an invitation. It didn't explain itself; it waited. And if you were willing to learn its language — cd, dir, copy, mkdir — it would do exactly what you asked. I didn't know it yet, but that was the first time a computer felt like a tool rather than a appliance you consumed.

Games, and the software underneath them​

I played the usual suspects. Wolfenstein 3D on a share so smeared the floppy disk never worked. Commander Keen, bouncing around a city that was obviously made by two people with a lot of coffee. Liero at 2 AM with a friend on a dial-up line. Prince of Persia, which taught me to save often because I was going to die a lot. Duke Nukem and the original Doom, and the specific magic of a shareware episode that ended exactly where the next one would begin.

But the thing that actually changed my life wasn't the games. It was the software around the games — and the fact that it was all just files on a disk.

I wrote my first .BAT file. I typed a command so long I broke the line and had to learn about line continuation. I opened a text editor, changed a line in a configuration file, and something behaved differently. I got a Blue Screen of Death and learned that a computer could fail, that failure had causes, and that I could go looking for them.

And then — the moment that turned into a career — I realized that a program was not magic. It was text. You could open it, read it, change it, break it, and build it back. Turbo Pascal, BASIC, the autoexec.bat, the config.sys: it all looked like the same thing wearing different costumes. A person had sat down and written instructions, and the machine obeyed.

That was the 启蒙 — the ignition. Software stopped being a black box and became a thing you could touch. Everything I have built since — the distributed systems, the Kubernetes clusters, the AI agents, this website — grew out of that one realization: a machine is not a magic box, it is a machine you can read.

Then the world moved into our pockets​

And then the world got a screen of its own.

Look at what a phone became. It is a camera, a wallet, a library, a newspaper, a game console, a map, a telephone, a bank, a hospital, a classroom. For most people alive today, the phone is the computer. It is where they read, work, play, learn, and think. It is where the entire center of gravity of computing moved.

And that means something quietly sad happened: the era where millions of people learned to command a machine is over. The DOS era wasn't just old — it was a way of learning that no longer has a doorway. That generation's first real contact with a computer was a blinking cursor asking what you wanted to do. Ours is a feed.

I don't think that's strictly worse. I'm not here to argue that a phone is a bad computer. But I do think it costs us something. An entire generation's sense of ownership over machines came from having to learn a command line. Nobody hands you a cursor anymore; you get a wall of rectangles and you never have to find out what's underneath.

So the question I kept asking myself was embarrassingly simple:

Why not bring DOS to the phone?

Not as a museum exhibit. Not as a nostalgia app that runs one demo in a webview. As a real thing — the genuine article, running on the actual machine in your pocket, with your own DOS games and software, the way it was meant to be used.

WhereQ-DOSBox​

This is the answer, and today I'm putting it in the open.

The welcome screen, a mounted drive, and the on-screen keyboard. Touch moves the DOS mouse; the keys type straight into DOSBox.

WhereQ-DOSBox is a native Android port of DOSBox — the emulator core runs as a real native library (libdosbox.so) inside an APK. Not a web page, not a WebView, not a JavaScript emulation of an x86 emulation. On your phone, at native speed.

A few things you can do with it today:

  • Run your own DOS software and games, from a mounted drive on your phone.
  • Type with the on-screen keyboard — the keys go straight into DOSBox.
  • Use the touchscreen as the DOS mouse.
  • Do all of it offline, with no account, no browser, and no tracking.

The APK is about 5.3 MB and runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 devices (Android 5.0 and newer).

It's open source — read it​

This is a GPL-2.0 project, and the DOSBox core is embedded with its AUTHORS, ChangeLog, COPYING and per-file headers intact, exactly as the license requires. The port touches the core in only four small, local places; everything else is upstream code.

I want to be honest about something: this post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository — the build guide, the porting log, the benchmark notes, and every line of the port are in the open, and I'd rather you read those than take my word for it.

👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox

To build it yourself:

git clone git@github.com:whereq/whereq-dosbox.git
cd whereq-dosbox
bin/build.sh all      # bootstrap + native + android + apk

That drops whereq-dosbox-debug.apk into build/apk/. The full guide — release signing, the Gradle path, the launcher icons — is in BUILDING.md.

Why I'm putting it out there​

Because I keep meeting people who remember the DOS era, and who want it back — but who had quietly accepted that it was gone, filed away with the beige tower and the 3.5-inch floppies.

It isn't gone. It's just been waiting for a port.

If this brings back one evening of C:\>, one afternoon of Commander Keen, one "oh — that's how it works" moment for somebody who never had a beige tower in the corner — then the months of porting were worth it.

If it brings back a memory for you too, I'd genuinely love to hear about it.

Thank you, DOSBox​

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project.

DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They made it compatible with a wide variety of DOS games, they kept it alive for three decades, and they did it as a gift to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft, and the generosity are entirely theirs.

This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which itself grew from Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. Every one of them pushed the "DOS in a browser" idea further than anyone thought possible — and that idea is exactly what made "DOS on a phone" something worth trying.

Thank you. All of it. DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team.

If you remember a specific game, or a specific machine, or a specific C:\> prompt — tell me. I am collecting them, and this is going to be a good archive.

entry.title: whereq.com 开源了：地图、爬虫，以及它读到的所有数据
entry.content:
一枚图钉，其实只是一句很小的话​

站在多伦多的一条街上，看着眼前这个门牌号，地图只会告诉你一句话：这里有一枚图钉。一家咖啡馆，一间医院，一所学校，也许还有一个停车场。

但一个地方本身是一大堆话，而图钉是其中最不重要的那句。

这个地址属于哪个学区 catchment？走路能到图书馆吗，是哪一家？街角加油站今天收 1.42 还是 1.79？这栋楼落在 ward 里、neighbourhood 里，还是两者都算？上周这条街上出过什么事？

这些答案每一条都是一份数据，而每一条都住在别的地方。学校边界在一个系统里，油价在另一个系统里，行政区划在第三个系统里，本地新闻又在第四个系统里。你看到的地图，不过是它们全部对齐之后的结果。

所以我把「对齐」这件事单独做成了一个层​

做这个应用的时候，最让我意外的是：真正的工作根本不在地图本身。

画图钉是简单的一半。难的一半是，地图本质上是一次 join。每一层都要有自己的键、自己的许可条款、自己的速率限制，还有自己对于「一个地方」的理解——而一个 POI（地址上的一个点）和一个行政区（把地址装进去的一个多边形），根本不是同一种东西，哪怕你可以随手把它们放在同一个下拉菜单里。

所以这个应用的第一版里躺着三个互不相干的抓取脚本，各自为自己的数据集而写，各自握着一把 API key，也各自在某个凌晨三点悄悄坏掉。

几乎世界上每一个应用都长成这个形状：十个应用，十个爬虫，十个每晚都会失败的作业。

解法是把「取数据」本身变成一个独立的层——一个进程、一个节奏、一处允许外部世界进入这个应用的口子。

我把它叫做爬虫，这是整个仓库里我最满意的部分。

爬虫​

地图上的一切，都是被爬下来的：
